This is the first meaning of the adjective derived from δέος [fear], which is said of persons and of things: whence arises a manifold use of the word for almost every kind of more serious evils, for expressing which the Latin words gravis [heavy] and vehemens [violent] and other more specific ones are very often suitable, which Stephanus used in interpreting passages of writers in his Thesaurus vol. 2 p. 953-954, such as atrox [fierce], indignus [unworthy], immanis [monstrous].
